messages:
julia (Customer): Hey team — we've got a bunch of users reporting they get logged out of our app intermittently after completing MFA. Happens across Chrome/Firefox on desktop and iOS Safari. Starts ~2 hours after we turned on 'remember device' for MFA. No browser console errors.

sara (Support): sorry you're hitting this — can you confirm org id and an example user id? also, does it occur on SSO or native auth? any repro steps? :eyes: 

julia (Customer): Org: acme-inc-42, user: julia@acme. It's SSO (Okta). Repro is flaky but I could reproduce consistently by: 1) login via SSO + complete MFA; 2) close browser tab; 3) open app in new tab -> sometimes shows logged out. Happened for 6/20 tries on Chrome.

sara (Support): thanks. I'm escalating to eng-security and SRE. Can you share the network request/response for the login session set-cookie if possible? a raw header snippet would help.

julia (Customer): here's the raw Set-Cookie from the login response (copied from dev tools):
```
Set-Cookie: rd_session=eyJ...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; Max-Age=2592000; SameSite=Lax; Domain=.app.acme.com
```
Note: our app is hosted under app.acme.com but we also embed the app in admin.acme.com via an iframe for certain flows.

mike (SRE): seeing correlated spikes in 401s from acme-inc-42 since the "remember device" rollout. Traces show session cookie not being sent back to server in some requests. Example from edge logs at 2026-03-15T15:12:03Z: 
```
request_id=xyz123 client_ip=10.20.30.40 host=app.acme.com path=/api/v1/generate status=401 reason="no_session_cookie"
```
Also see auth-service logs: `session_lookup: cookie_present=false for user=julia@acme` followed by `auth_result=prompt_mfa`.

arpit (Eng-Security): quick hypothesis: when we added the "remember device" flow we introduced a cookie rotation path that writes a migrated cookie with `SameSite=Lax`. For cross-site usage (embedded in admin.acme.com iframe) that will get dropped in modern browsers unless `SameSite=None; Secure` is set. Because the cookie was issued with Lax, the browser won't send it on a cross-site context for POST requests from the iframe. That matches the intermittent nature (some flows are same-site, others cross-site).

sara (Support): that makes sense — customer said embedding via iframe. Is that a config we can change non-disruptively?

arpit (Eng-Security): yes. Root cause: migration handler in auth-service (cookie_migration.go) sets samesite by reading legacy flag; if legacy flag absent it defaults to Lax. We should explicitly set `SameSite=None` for migrated persistent session cookies when the app domain is a superdomain of the embedding domain or when `remember_device=true`. Patch attached below. Repro steps I used locally:
1) Start auth-service with cookie defaults (SameSite=Lax)
2) Issue login in main-site context -> cookie set 
3) Load iframe from admin subdomain -> cookie not sent -> 401

Curl reproduction (iframe-like, cross-site):
```
# simulate cross-site request by setting Referer header
curl -i -H "Host: app.acme.com" -H "Referer: https://admin.acme.com/dashboard" https://app.acme.com/api/v1/session
```
Expected: session cookie included on request. Observed: not included by browser (can't truly emulate browser behaviour with curl but logs show auth-service sees no cookie).

arpit (Eng-Security): proposed patch (pseudo):
```
- cookie.SameSite = http.SameSiteLaxMode
+ // remember-device and iframe contexts require cross-site cookie
+ cookie.SameSite = http.SameSiteNoneMode
+ cookie.Secure = true
```
Also update cookie header to explicitly include `SameSite=None` string for older clients.

mike (SRE): timeline/impact? can we roll this without invalidating all sessions? we want minimal churn.

arpit (Eng-Security): plan: add compatibility behavior in auth-service: when rotating cookie name, write both cookies for a 48h overlap window — new cookie named `rd_session_v2` with `SameSite=None; Secure; HttpOnly` and keep `rd_session` for backward compatibility (still readable server-side). After 48h remove old cookie. This avoids forcing reauth for active users. Migration pseudo:
```
Set-Cookie: rd_session_v2=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=None; Max-Age=2592000; Domain=.app.acme.com
Set-Cookie: rd_session=...; Path=/; HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Lax; Max-Age=2592000; Domain=.app.acme.com
```
Auth service should prefer `rd_session_v2` if present, otherwise fall back to `rd_session`.

sara (Support): that sounds good. Customer wants to know if they need to change anything on their side — embedding will work after patch?

arpit (Eng-Security): yes, once the cookie is set with `SameSite=None; Secure` browsers will include it for cross-site contexts (iframes) so embedding should stop breaking. No action required from customer's side. We'll notify them when canary is complete.

mike (SRE): rollout proposal: deploy patch to auth-service canaries (10% of hosts) immediately, monitor 401 rate and session_create metrics for 2 hours. If no regression, expand to 50% for 1h, then 100% next low-traffic window. Migration: issue both cookies for 48h as described. The only risk is duplicate cookies causing slight increase in cookie header size, negligible.

deploy-bot: deploy started -> auth-service v1.4.7-canary -> hosts impacted: auth-canary-1..3

arpit (Eng-Security): I'll open a quick PR with the change and include the migration window logic, plus an opt-out flag in config `auth.cookie.migration_overlap_hours`. PR link: (internal) https://git.redwood/eng/auth-service/pulls/812

sara (Support): assigned follow-ups:
- @arpit to land patch and coordinate canary (ETA 2h)
- @mike to monitor rollout metrics and rollback if 401s spike (ETA ongoing)
- @sara to notify Julia and provide suggested messaging and support KB article (ETA 4h)

julia (Customer): incredible turnaround, appreciate the quick action. Please ping when canary passes so we can verify on our side. :pray:

arpit (Eng-Security): note for postmortem: add an integration test for cookie behavior in cross-site contexts (iframe + referer) and add test for cookie rotation preserving SameSite for remember-device flows.

mike (SRE): canary metrics after 30m: auth 401 rate for acme-inc-42 dropped from 3.2% -> 0.7% on canary hosts, session_create rate stable. No error spikes in logs. Proceeding to 50% in 30m.

deploy-bot: deploy expanded -> auth-service v1.4.7 -> 50% hosts

arpit (Eng-Security): merged PR and added migration flag defaults to 48h. Will follow up with a short note for the infra runbook about cookie size considerations.

sara (Support): Julia — we rolled to 50% and are monitoring. Can you try reproducing now? If you still see it, send a network trace and we can escalate to a full rollback if needed.

julia (Customer): I just tested on Chrome and iOS Safari embedding — flow looks stable on 3/3 tries. Huge thanks.

sara (Support): marking this thread as "in progress" until 48h post-migration. We'll post a final summary then.

arpit (Eng-Security): post-action list: add tests, update docs (cookie migration KB), schedule a 48h follow-up check, and create internal ticket to remove old cookie after overlap window. I'll own the remove-old-cookie job.

mike (SRE): noted. I'll keep monitoring. closing if no regressions after 48h.

sara (Support): thanks all. closing notes will include timeline and public KB for customers embedding app in subdomains. :white_check_mark:
